az_7_upper_highway.blurb: Upper Highway is the high end of the Mount Lemmon road in the Santa Catalina Mountains above Tucson, starting around milepost 19 at the Palisades and running up toward the summit, near 8,000 feet. Sport routes lead, boulder problems come close behind, and there is a solid trad contingent. Roped climbs cluster around 5.10 to 5.12 with a thin scattering of easier lines, while the bouldering runs from the gentlest problems up through the double-digit V grades. The granite along this highway is pale, muscovite-bearing and heavily fractured and jointed. Winter brings cold and snow, which shortens the season up here, and the upper mountain holds some of the longest, most committing routes on Lemmon. Reef of Rocks, Aspen Trail Boulders and Wilderness of Rocks are its biggest sub-areas.

ma_western_ma.blurb: Western Massachusetts holds a spread of gneiss crags and boulder fields, from Northfield in the north down into the Berkshires near the Connecticut line. Bouldering makes up the largest share, with trad and sport roughly level and a little top-roping. Most roped climbs fall between 5.7 and 5.12 with a few harder ones, and the boulder problems favor the lower and middle V grades. Rose Ledge is a 40 to 60 foot cliff of gneiss with horizontal cracks, strong on moderates and often top-roped. Hanging Mountain, in Sandisfield, is a southeast-facing band about 1,000 feet long with crags from 60 to 240 feet, built from a mix of granite, gneiss and schist that still sheds loose stone. Quality and crowds vary a lot from one crag to the next, so some spots stay quiet.

tn_stone_fort_aka_little_rock_city.blurb: Stone Fort, also called Little Rock City, is a sandstone bouldering area in oak and rhododendron woods near Chattanooga, set beside a golf course. The boulders sit close together, so walking between problems is short. It is almost entirely bouldering, with just a couple of roped routes. Grades start at the easiest problems and reach the low double digits, but most of the climbing sits between V1 and V7, so there is plenty for newer boulderers and a good number of hard lines. Expect many overhanging problems that reward finger strength and careful footwork, plus technical slabs that test balance. Summers are hot; early mornings keep the rock cooler, while afternoon sun improves friction at the cost of sweat. Stone Fort Bouldering holds most of the problems, with Back Nine next.

ca_sequoia_kings_canyon_np.blurb: The two national parks pair granite domes and big walls with a large bouldering scene. Trad and bouldering share the top spot, followed by a smaller group of alpine and sport routes. Roped grades center on 5.9 to 5.11, with a few easier and harder, and the problems mostly fall between V0 and V5. The granite is often compared to Yosemite for quality. Moro Rock, near Giant Forest, is the easiest big face to reach, with a west side offering about 1,000 vertical feet of cracks and knobs. Angel Wings is one of the largest walls at roughly 2,000 feet but is remote, and most climbs in the parks need at least a day of hiking. Bubbs Creek has multi-pitch domes. Sub-areas include SEKI Bouldering, Kings Canyon and Moro Rock.

wv_eastern_wv.blurb: Eastern West Virginia is a highland region of limestone sport crags and scattered boulders, within an hour of Seneca Rocks. Sport climbing leads, bouldering follows, and trad and top-rope routes fill out the rest. Roped grades run mainly from 5.8 to 5.12 and peak around 5.9 and 5.10, with a handful easier and harder; problems are mostly V0 to V4. Smoke Hole Canyon, between Franklin and Petersburg, has limestone walls about 70 feet tall and well over a hundred routes, mostly needing six to ten quickdraws. Reeds Creek, near the Smoke Hole entrance, is a smaller limestone wall of about 60 feet with mostly 5.7 to 5.11 lines; it faces south and takes sun all day, which makes it a good winter choice. Camp 70 Boulders adds high-country bouldering.

oh_southwest_ohio.blurb: Southwest Ohio climbing is dominated by bouldering, with sport routes, a good amount of top-roping and a little trad. Roped grades lean toward 5.8 to 5.12 and boulder problems mostly sit at V0 to V4. Mad River Gorge near Springfield is the largest climbing area in the state, running along about a half mile of cliffside with sport, trad and bouldering from roughly 5.6 to 5.12 and V0 to V7. Paint Creek State Park offers a dolomite wall roughly 70 yards long that stays in shade all day, mostly top-rope lines from easy up to about 5.9 plus a number of boulder problems.
